questions.stem: Which observation is seen when potassium reacts with water but NOT when lithium reacts with water?

options.text: The metal catches fire with a lilac flame

questions.explanation: Potassium is more reactive than lithium, so it reacts more vigorously with water. Potassium catches fire immediately with a lilac flame due to the exothermic reaction, while lithium only fizzes steadily without igniting. Both float and produce hydrogen gas.
